Topic.label: Central Symmetry and Centrally Symmetric Figures

Question: Which of the following statements about “central symmetry” and “centrally symmetric figures” is correct?

Choices.A: Central symmetry is a relationship between two figures, while being centrally symmetric is a property of a single figure.
Choices.B: The two terms have exactly the same meaning, with no difference.
Choices.C: A centrally symmetric figure is a figure that coincides with itself after a \(90^\circ\) rotation about a point.

Solution: Central symmetry describes two figures that coincide with each other after a \(180^\circ\) rotation about a point. A centrally symmetric figure coincides with itself after a \(180^\circ\) rotation about a point.
